swarajya.name: Shivaji's Forces (early Swarajya)

historical.text: The player leads the polity built around Shivaji, which grew from a base in the Pune highlands in the 1640s into a significant regional power by the late 1650s. The Adil Shahi state was the dominant neighbour. The name Swarajya is used by the game as a title; how early and in what sense contemporaries used the concept is debated.
sources: Sarkar, Jadunath. Shivaji and His Times

swarajya.gameplay_note: No artillery recruitment in this slice: a gameplay constraint representing limited early resources, not a claim that no guns existed.

adilshahi.name: Adil Shahi Sultanate (Bijapur)

historical.text: The Deccan sultanate ruled from Bijapur by the Adil Shahi dynasty. Mohammad Adil Shah reigned 1627-1656. The Adil Shahi state was the dominant regional power around Pune in the 1640s.
sources: Eaton, Richard M. A Social History of the Deccan, 1300-1761 (Cambridge, 2005)

adilshahi.gameplay_note: Controlled by the computer. Its forces here are generic gameplay armies, not reconstructions of named field commands.

maratha_state.name: Maratha State (Shahu and the Peshwa)

historical.text: The Maratha state under Chhatrapati Shahu (reigned 1707-1749) at Satara, with the Peshwa as chief minister and leader of its armies. Baji Rao I was Peshwa from 1720 to 1740.

maratha_state.gameplay_note: Fast cavalry and mobile campaigning are favoured by the commanders' modifiers; numbers are abstractions.

historical.text: The Deccan state founded by Nizam-ul-Mulk Asaf Jah I, who became effectively autonomous in the 1720s while nominally under the Mughal emperor.
sources: Eaton, Richard M. A Social History of the Deccan, 1300-1761 (Cambridge, 2005)

mughal.name: Mughal Empire

historical.text: The Mughal Empire under Muhammad Shah (reigned 1719-1748), still large and wealthy but with weakening control over distant provinces in the 1730s.

mughal.gameplay_note: Computer-controlled, defensive and rich, but its provinces are far from its capital.

maratha_confederacy.name: Maratha Leaders (Peshwa and allies)

historical.text: In 1817-18 the Peshwa Baji Rao II, the Bhonsle of Nagpur and Holkar each fought the East India Company, largely separately. The game merges them into one faction, a gameplay simplification.

maratha_confederacy.gameplay_note: One faction stands in for several historically separate rulers.

eic.name: East India Company

historical.text: The East India Company's Bombay, Madras and Bengal armies, made up largely of Indian sepoys under British officers, were the main opponent of the Marathas in the Anglo-Maratha Wars (1775-1818).

eic.gameplay_note: Computer-controlled. Rich and well supplied, with strong drilled infantry.
